title: PRD - Service Level Staircase: tenant-priority decay, hysteresis windows, and staged-cutover rules
creator: Ariel Santos
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable SLO contract and rollout gating scheme we call the 'Service Level Staircase' to support multi-tenant, multi-model routing. This ticket captures the product requirements, acceptance criteria, monitoring surface, and phased rollout rules for per-tenant weighted SLOs with a priority decay function and hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation during short spikes. The Staircase is intended for high-variability workloads where tenants have distinct latency and availability commitments and where model fallbacks or degraded modes may be applied.

Scope:
- Define SLO metrics (latency envelopes, availability) and how they map to tenant priority levels (gold/silver/bronze plus dynamic priority boosts).
- Specify error budget calculation and the 'priority decay' algorithm that discounts short-lived spikes for high-priority tenants while letting lower priority tenants be throttled earlier.
- Design hysteresis windows and staged-cutover rules for canary -> ramp -> global rollout to prevent destructive rollbacks and oscillation.
- List concrete rollout gates (metric thresholds, burn-rate windows, observability checks) and automated rollback conditions.
- Compose acceptance tests, dashboards, and alerts required before canary expansion.

Out of scope: deep infra implementation details for kernel-level throttles (ENG will own), quota UI changes (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions: for conversational chat endpoints define p50/p95/p99 latency buckets and availability target for each priority tier: gold: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 520ms, availability >= 99.95%; silver: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms, availability >= 99.9%; bronze: p95 <= 700ms, p99 <= 2000ms, availability >= 99.5%.

Error budget calculation: compute rolling 30-day error budget for availability and a 1-hour burn-rate window for latency regressions. Error budget consumption must support per-tenant weighted accounting (weight = priority_score * active_sessions).

Priority decay algorithm: implement formula that reduces a tenant's effective priority score by 50% for 10 minutes after sustained high burn-rate, with configurable hysteresis windows (default 5/10/30m) to avoid flip-flopping.

Hysteresis & staged-cutover gates: canary at 1% traffic for 30m with no more than 5% relative loss in p95; ramp to 10% for 2 hours with burn-rate < 2x baseline; global rollout allowed only when 24h aggregated burn < 1% and no critical alerts triggered.

Automated rollback: trigger immediate rollback if canary p99 worsens by > 40% and error budget burn exceeds 5% in the 1h window, or if availability drops below target for the tier for 15 consecutive minutes.
Observability: required dashboards and alerts (listed below) are provisioned and linked, and synthetic probes covering typical prompt lengths exist in three regions.
Operational playbook: runbook exists describing steps for manual override, tenant-exclusion, and emergency cutback to safety lanes.
monitoring: Dashboard: Service Level Staircase overview (per-tenant p50/p95/p99 + availability + error budget remaining).
Alert: Canary p95 regression > 5% relative vs baseline for 10m -> severity P1 oncall page.
Alert: 1h burn-rate > 3x expected -> auto-notify SRE + PM.
Synthetic probes: 5 probes per region that exercise typical prompt mix (short, medium, long).
Tracing: distributed traces surfaced for slow tail tokens with links to KV cache hit/miss rates and batching histograms.
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (pre-canary): unit tests + CI integration checks green, observability dashboards deployed, synthetic probes healthy for 48h.
Gate 1 (canary 1%): run 30m, must meet p95 regression < 5% and error-budget burn < 1% in 1h window.
Gate 2 (ramp 10%): run 2h, burn-rate < 2x baseline and no critical alerts. If fire, pause and collect traces for 1h before retry.
Gate 3 (regional staging): expand to 25% in a second region for 6h with no availability regressions and stable tail behavior.
Gate 4 (global rollout): 24h aggregated error budget usage < 1% and post-deployment canary synthetic success >= 99.5% in each region.
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — agreed to use weighted error budgets to prioritize gold tenants during transient overloads. Action: ENG to propose weight computation by 2026-02-20.

2026-02-20: ENG proposal received — weight = base_priority_score * sqrt(active_sessions). Trade-off: sqrt reduces sensitivity to large session spikes; PM prefers linear for predictability. Decision: keep sqrt for initial rollout and revisit after 1 month of telemetry.

2026-02-25: Design review — UX requested explicit messaging for tenants moved to degraded mode; add API flag 'degradation_reason' to responses. ENG raised concern about payload bloat; compromise: short code + link to tenant status page.
2026-02-28: SRE requested hysteresis defaults be conservative (10/15/30m) to avoid oscillation on noisy probes; PM accepts but keeps 5/10/30m as configurable defaults in PRD.
2026-03-01: Draft dashboards merged to staging (link below). PM to run tabletop incident playbook with SRE and support on 2026-03-05.
